name: Malachi
author: Almost nothing is known about the writer beyond the name Malachi, which means 'my messenger' in Hebrew. Tradition treats it as the personal name of a prophet, someone called to speak God's word to the people. Many scholars think it may instead be a title drawn from a phrase later in the book, leaving the prophet unnamed. Either way, he was clearly someone who knew the temple, its priests and its worship well.
audience: The book was first addressed to the Jewish community in and around Jerusalem, especially the priests who served at the rebuilt temple. They were a small, poor community under foreign rule, and many had grown tired and doubtful as the hopes stirred by their return from exile seemed to go unfulfilled.
era: The book is usually dated to around 460 to 430 BC, when Judah was a minor province of the vast Persian Empire, ruled by a Persian-appointed governor. Jewish exiles had been allowed home from Babylon about a century earlier, and the temple had been rebuilt by around 516 BC. Worship had resumed, but enthusiasm had faded. The book is often placed close to the time of Ezra and Nehemiah, leaders who faced many of the same problems.

notes.1:2: Edom, the neighbouring nation descended from Esau, had gloated over Jerusalem's fall in 586 BC and was itself being overrun and pushed from its homeland around this time.
notes.2:10: Marriages to women who worshipped other gods, and the breakup of marriages, were problems Ezra and Nehemiah also confronted in Jerusalem during this era.
notes.4:4: Horeb is another name for Mount Sinai; these closing lines end the collection known as the Twelve Prophets and, in most Christian Bibles, the whole Old Testament.

flags.problem: Ezra and Nehemiah did confront marriages to women who worshipped other gods, but they did not confront 'the breakup of marriages' as a problem. Ezra in fact required men to send away their foreign wives. Pairing divorce with them as a shared problem is misleading.
flags.suggestion: Limit the Ezra–Nehemiah link to mixed marriages, e.g. 'Marriages to women who worshipped other gods were a problem Ezra and Nehemiah also confronted in Jerusalem during this era; the book also speaks of men divorcing their wives.'

flags.problem: 'The collection known as the Twelve Prophets' may puzzle ordinary readers, who usually know these books as the 'Minor Prophets' and may not realise they were once grouped as a single collection.
flags.suggestion: Add a short gloss, e.g. 'the collection known as the Twelve Prophets (often called the Minor Prophets, Hosea to Malachi)'.
